title: OTLP header & sampling preservation adapter with tenant-consent retention and S3 archival fallback
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: We currently lose user/tenant sampling decisions and a portion of tracing metadata during protocol translation between OTLP/gRPC ingest and downstream Tempo/Jaeger sinks. This causes inconsistent trace sampling across backends, complicates retention enforcement per customer consent policy, and makes S3 archival of long-tail traces brittle under spikes.

Goal: Implement an OTLP adapter that preserves sampling flags and important headers across translation, enforces tenant-consent retention gating, and provides an S3 archival fallback (cold path) that is backpressure-aware to protect Tempo ingest during bursts. The adapter should be pluggable in the ingress path so both hosted and dedicated clusters can opt-in.

Approach:
- Build a lightweight transform layer that sits after auth/token validation and before the existing OTLP fanout. Responsibilities:
  - Normalize and persist sampling attributes (sampled flag, sampling.priority, trace-propagation headers) into a canonical envelope field so downstream exporters can make consistent decisions.
  - Attach tenant retention metadata (consent_status, retention_tier) derived from tenant profile service.
  - Implement an async S3 archival writer for spans tagged as "retain-long-term"; when Tempo is healthy the adapter will route primary copies to Tempo and enqueue an archival copy; when Tempo backpressure detected (latency/queue depth thresholds), the adapter drains primary to S3 with throttled writes and emits throttled metrics.
  - Provide per-tenant throttling and quota checks so customer isolation is preserved.

Design trade-offs and rationale:
- Keeping the adapter as a sidecar/filter reduces changes to Tempo and existing exporters. Sidecar model adds deployment complexity for on-prem customers; we'll offer both sidecar and in-process middleware variants.
- Canonical envelope increases payload size slightly but guarantees sampling and retention fidelity; we compress envelope fields in the S3 archival path.
- S3 archival as fallback reduces data loss risk but raises cold storage costs; we gate archival with tenant consent and retention tier.

Out of scope:
- Full trace rehydration/replay from S3 for immediate query (future work).
- Changing sampling algorithms across clients.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sampling parity: end-to-end sampled=true traces from instrumented clients remain sampled=true when observed in Tempo and S3 for 99.9% of test traces.
- Retention gate: traces flagged as "do-not-retain" per tenant profile are not written to S3 in acceptance tests.
- Backpressure behavior: under synthetic load that simulates 2x normal Tempo latency and queue fill, primary write success to Tempo remains >= 95% until configured threshold, after which archival to S3 is reliably used.
- Metrics: expose per-tenant metrics (archival_count, tempo_failover_count, adapter_latency_p95) and dashboards updated.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged deploy to a canary host (internal telemetry tenant) for 48h.
2) Gradual ramp to 5% of tenants with detailed tracing assertions.
3) Add tenants keyed by retention tiers for 24h soak.
4) Flip default for hosted environment after 1 week of stable telemetry.

Monitoring & alerts:
- Pager if tempo_failover_count spikes > 10/min for any region for 10m.
- Alert on adapter_latency_p95 > 500ms.
- Daily job to spot-check sampling parity by replaying golden traces.

Acceptance test harness: see design doc (Confluence) and unit/integration tests in repo. Performance target: adapter adds <15ms median and <120ms p99 overhead under nominal load.

Notes on privacy/compliance: retention gating reads consent status from tenant profile which accesses PII-light flags only; archival encryption uses customer KMS when present.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Initial kickoff: scoped core responsibilities and agreed sidecar + middleware variants. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/OTLP+Sampling+Preservation+Adapter
2026-02-26 - Spike complete: prototyped envelope field and confirmed no change required to Tempo ingestion in dev. Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/otel-adapter/pull/112

2026-03-01 - Security review notes: key rotation for S3 writer required; Marcus to add KMS integration. Ticket: SEC-44 referenced. Decision: use envelope-level AES-GCM with per-tenant KMS when available.

2026-03-03 - Perf run: adapter median latency 9ms, p99 87ms at 2000 rps with batching; memory footprint +30MB on small sidecar. Benchmark artifacts: https://ci.redwood.com/artifacts/obs/ENG-814907/perf-20260303

2026-03-04 - PR opened for adapter core, tagging infra and storage owners for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/otel-adapter/pull/154 - awaiting infra approval for S3 writer IAM policy changes.
2026-03-05 - Next steps: implement per-tenant throttling, wire tenant-profile lookup cache, add E2E test that verifies sampling parity across Tempo and S3. Assigned to Marcus Chen.
